the following issues: (a) How much can be achieved by a single learner? (b) How much can we expect to achieve by a team of learners?
the following questions: (1) How much can we gain in terms of computational power by using teams instead of single machines? (2) How much can be gained by using teams of different size?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
team learning of computable languages is possible, but it is not always more powerful than individual learning.
the results on team learning are not significantly better than those on single-machine learning.
the team learning of computable languages is not more powerful than individual learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results for team learning of recursive languages are very similar to the corresponding results for team learning for recursively enumerable languages.
the redundancy issue has been resolved and the aggregation issue has been resolved in some cases.
the redundancy and aggregation issues are not very interesting in the context of learning computable languages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the team setting is more powerful than the individual setting for learning computable languages.
team learning of computable languages is not much harder than individual learning of computable (and even recursive) languages.
team learning is a viable approach to studying computable language learning.
